text:
sara_support: FYI incoming escalation from AcmeHealth — they report a clear uptick in hallucinations / factual errors since we rolled the v2.2 quantized variant yesterday. Customer says prompts that used to be stable are now inventing citations and dates. They flagged it as SEV-2 atm.

sara_support: Customer provided minimal repro: they call our chat endpoint with model redwood-v2.2-q4 (rolled 2024-06-12 22:34 UTC). Sample prompt they shared: 

```
User: "Summarize Dr. Patel's 2021 cardiology guideline on beta-blocker dosing for atrial fibrillation. Include page references and study names."
```

sara_support: Their prior output on redwood-v2.1-ff16 (before rollout) was concise and referenced real trials. On v2.2-q4 the assistant returned: 

```
Assistant: "According to the 2020 CardioStudy (p. 42) and the Patel et al. 2021 guideline, beta-blockers should be initiated at 50mg and titrated to 200mg..."
```

sara_support: Customer claims those citations don’t exist and the dose numbers are wrong. They attached request ids and timestamps: 2024-06-13T08:11:09Z (req id acme-req-7743). Said it started right after the 2.2 rollout. Requesting rollback or mitigations + SOC/SEC confirmation that no user data was exposed.

jon_ml: Thanks — adding context. I saw higher divergence on our small internal eval for factuality post-quant rollout but it wasn't massive. Need more samples from the customer. @sara_support can you paste 3 full request/response pairs (raw JSON with headers) and the request_id for each? Also need model binary tag & exact weight config (canary %) from deploy.

sara_support: Pasted below one full convo they gave (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
model: redwood-v2.2-q4
input: [the user prompt above]
response: {"id":"acme-7743","text":"According to the 2020 CardioStudy (p. 42) and the Patel et al. 2021 guideline..."}
```

sara_support: They also included a direct diff: prior version answered with a short summary + links to pubmed IDs. New version makes up "CardioStudy" and cites page numbers. Very reproducible for them.

jon_ml: Got it. @deploy-bot can you confirm exact rollout timeline and traffic split for redwood-v2.2-q4 in prod for the acme region? I want commit hash and quantization config.

deploy-bot: Deployment event: redwood-v2.2-q4 promoted to prod at 2024-06-12T22:34:12Z. Traffic policy: global canary 30% -> 100% in EU/NA within 45m. Commit: a1b2c3f. Quantization: int4-llm-q4_0.

matt_oncall: If this is causing hallucinations we should consider routing affected customers back to v2.1 while ML investigates. Revert is low-risk if we do weighted routing. @lee_product do we have a pre-approved rollback policy for paid customers?

lee_product: We typically coordinate with account team first, but for severe regressions we can do emergency revert at infra level and notify after. We need to confirm customer scope: is it all requests or only specific end-users/doc types?

sara_support: AcmeHealth says it’s across docs when asking for clinical guidance and citations. They run a large QA pipeline, so this is high impact for them. They've asked for immediate mitigation. They also asked for an incident ticket and ETA.

jon_ml: Action plan: 1) get 5 reproducible examples from customer (we have 1). 2) run those against v2.1 and v2.2 on our staging harness to confirm delta. 3) run targeted eval for hallucination metrics (factuality F1 / hallucination rate) across these prompts. 4) if delta > threshold (we use 7% absolute increase) -> recommend routing back to v2.1 for that org and start patch rolling.

jon_ml: Quick repro I ran locally on same commit: using their prompt truncated to 256 tokens, v2.1 returns passage with two PubMed IDs; v2.2 returns invented trial names. Suspect quantization-induced degradation for long-context citation retrieval or prompt-conditioning.

infra-bot: Notice: we can apply per-customer model routing. Command snippet: 
```
redwood-cli routes update --org acmehealth --model redwood-v2.1-ff16 --weight 100
```

matt_oncall: If we decide to flip routing, do it during low-traffic window and throttle to avoid cold-start latency spikes. Also watch token throughput. I'll schedule a 15m window and run health checks after.

lee_product: Also notify account team and legal about potential regulatory impact (medical domain). CC: customer success manager. We'll prepare a customer-facing note: apology, timeline, mitigation, and promise to run regression suite and share results.

sara_support: Putting this into an incident now. Creating ticket INC-2024-ACME-09 and assigning to @jon_ml and @matt_oncall. Customer wants rollback first. They asked specifically: "Is there any chance you changed model knowledge or training data?" — we must answer: no training/data change, only quantization and small kernel optimizations.

jon_ml: Confirming: no training-data changes; only a quantization build and runtime kernel selection change. That can affect factual output in edge cases. We’ll prioritize a quick A/B on their prompts and if confirmed, enable per-org routing to v2.1.

sara_support: Customer asked for immediate workaround in the meantime: either rollback or a prompt-engineering shim (we can prepend a safety directive + request for citations). They prefer rollback.

matt_oncall: I'll prepare the routing flip. Before action, @jon_ml please paste the exact staging command you want us to run to validate. Also include what monitoring metrics to watch (hallucination rate, error rate, tail latency).

jon_ml: Staging command I used: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v2.2-q4","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Run same with model redwood-v2.1-ff16. Metrics: automated NER-based fact-check mismatch rate, and manual spot check of citation PPV. Also check generation token distribution (we saw odd token repetition before).

infra-bot: Routing change ready: run `redwood-cli routes update --org acmehealth --model redwood-v2.1-ff16 --weight 100 --dry-run` to preview.

sara_support: I'll tell AcmeHealth we can do an emergency per-org rollback while we investigate. I'll ask for 4 more examples and upload to the incident ticket.

lee_product: Good. After rollback, we should schedule a post-mortem and add this scenario to Redwood Optimize checks (quantization regression on citation tasks).
